name: Full population, Balkir et al.
description: All taxes paid by US residents divided by their economic income; 183 million tax units

name: Full population, Splinter
description: Transfers added to income and refundable tax credits subtracted from taxes

name: Count transfers as income, refundable credits as negative taxes
description: Adds government transfers such as Social Security to income ($21.4tn to $25.1tn a year) and subtracts refundable tax credits from taxes ($6.46tn to $6.28tn)

name: Top 400, Balkir et al.
description: Wealthiest 0.0002% of tax units, 367 on average; range: the study's sensitivity tests

name: Remove “pure” capital gains from income
description: Takes realized price gains on shares (about $20bn of $166bn a year) out of income as double counting of profits; the tax paid on them stays in

name: Split family fortunes across tax returns
description: Spreads Forbes family fortunes over spouses and adult children: 39% less income and 21% less tax for the top tax units; other splits give +4 to +13

name: Add likely missing state income taxes
description: Assumes the top 400's state income taxes grew with their income after the 2018 cap on deducting them: $17bn rather than the $11bn reported

name: Top 400, Splinter
description: Top 400 after Splinter's three adjustments; range: his alternative splits of family wealth
